stem.text: A metal wire is attached at one end to a fixed point and a load is hung from the other end so that the wire hangs vertically. The load is increased from zero to $20\,\text{N}$. This causes the wire to extend elastically by $5.0\,\text{mm}$. The load is then reduced to $12\,\text{N}$ and the extension decreases to $3.0\,\text{mm}$.

stem.alt: Load against extension graph: a straight line from the origin rising to load 20 N at extension 5.0 mm, with arrows showing loading upwards; a dashed line marks load 12 N at extension 3.0 mm on the return path, with an arrow showing unloading back down the same line to the origin

stem.text: How much strain energy is released during the unloading process?
